improvements.title: Core files reach the index
improvements.problem: max_file_kb = 300 silently kept HeidiSQL's main.pas and dbconnection.pas and commons-lang's StringUtils.java out of the index: the very files that change most.
improvements.fix: A 2 MB default limit, and every run reports what it left out and why.
improvements.evidence: HeidiSQL went from 1,573 to 2,065 chunks, and 5 core files came back to the index.

improvements.title: Delphi the grammar cannot read
improvements.problem: 44 of 189 units gave parse errors. dbconnection.pas lost 43% of its routines, and chunks cut methods in half.
improvements.fix: When the grammar fails, a scan of routines and types sets chunk boundaries and symbols.

improvements.title: Folders that looked like build output
improvements.problem: Folders named target, build or Win32 were skipped even with real sources: a Java package org/acme/target, or Lazarus sources in win32/.
improvements.fix: These folders only count as build output outside the source root, and Win32 only together with Debug or Release.
improvements.evidence: Covered by unit tests with the real paths.

improvements.title: Lexical ranking by rarity
improvements.problem: Words such as how, the and is weighed as much as circuit. Without stemming, escaped did not find EscapeString.
improvements.fix: BM25-style weight by rarity, English and Portuguese stopwords, light stemming, and extra weight for path and symbol.
improvements.evidence: Lexical only, on dev: MRR 0.65, against 0.42 for grep.

improvements.title: Whole-file list
improvements.problem: A chunk rarely holds every word of a question. On huge units, grep won by looking at the whole file.
improvements.fix: Files holding the most query weight join the fusion through their best chunk.
improvements.evidence: The largest single contribution on dev: MRR from 0.59 to 0.65.

improvements.title: References instead of dropped hits
improvements.problem: The token budget threw good results away.
improvements.fix: What does not fit comes back as path, lines and symbol.
improvements.evidence: Recall@10 from 0.76 to 0.83 on dev, for about 220 tokens.

improvements.title: New MCP tools
improvements.problem: No answer to who calls X, no map of huge files, and no way to read code outside this disk.
improvements.fix: find_references, file_outline and read_code. find_symbol takes TOrder.Cancel and matches part of a name.
improvements.evidence: On dev, caller questions dropped to about 420 tokens.

improvements.title: The agent started using the index
improvements.problem: With the original AGENTS.md note, the real agent never called Ragnar: 0 of 2 measured runs used the index, with the server up.
improvements.fix: The project note, the server instructions and the search_code description now say when to start with the index.
improvements.evidence: 33 of 34 dev runs called Ragnar after the change.

improvements.title: Smaller default budget
improvements.problem: At 4,000 tokens per search, the real agent spent 37% more context than with grep.
improvements.fix: A default of 5 hits within 2,000 tokens.
improvements.evidence: On dev, median context from 34.2k to 27.8k, against 25.1k for grep.

improvements.title: Reindexing without paying for embeddings again
improvements.problem: Any settings or chunker change reprocessed every vector. On a CPU, that costs hours.
improvements.fix: Vectors reused by content hash, and texts sent to the embedder by length.
improvements.evidence: Reindexing jsoup took 84 s, against 543 s from zero.

improvements.title: Secrets in fixtures
improvements.problem: One gitleaks finding stopped the whole repository.
improvements.fix: index.secret_action = "skip" leaves only those files out. The default stays fail.
improvements.evidence: 3 of the 8 repositories would have stopped.

improvements.title: Chunks and errors
improvements.problem: Chunks of up to 96,000 characters, 293 of 608 Serilog chunks with no symbol, and a 4xx from the embedder with no clear message.
improvements.fix: Huge nodes split, whole-file chunks name their declarations and namespace, and errors are clear.
improvements.evidence: Serilog went from 293 to 8 chunks with no symbol, and HeidiSQL's largest chunk from 17,330 to 2,778 characters.

experiments.name: Vector and lexical weights at 1.5
experiments.decision: Weights stay at 1, with no fine tuning on noise.

experiments.name: Model jina-code, MiniLM, multilingual
experiments.result: MRR 0.68, 0.64 and 0.57. In Portuguese: 0.77, 0.31 and 0.38. MiniLM indexes about 3 times faster.
experiments.decision: jina-code stays the default. MiniLM is the option for weak CPUs.

experiments.name: PT to EN glossary
experiments.decision: Dropped: it does not pay for 150 lines of vocabulary.

experiments.name: Budget with a real agent
experiments.decision: 2,000 is the new default. Below that, the agent compensates with grep.

experiments.name: Embedding speed on CPU
experiments.result: Between 2 and 2.6 chunks/s with 6, 10 or 20 threads, and with up to 5 processes.
experiments.decision: The bottleneck is the machine. Sorting by length and reusing vectors were the real gains.

limits: The token difference of the scripted arms, 56k against 2.2k, does not hold for a real agent. Agents use grep with partial reads, which costs far less than that model assumes. For cost, trust the real agent section.

The agent gets almost everything right in both modes on these repositories, which have between 100 and 500 indexed files. They do not show where an index should help most: large codebases, and several codebases at once.

On cross-file flow and Portuguese questions, the right file usually comes back, but the snippet with the evidence does not always fit in 2,000 tokens. On flow, the evidence reached the context in 2 of 8 questions, against 5 of 8 for grep. The agent still has to read the file.
The agent's correct-answer rule is simple: cite an expected file. It does not judge the quality of the explanation.
Curated questions were written by reading the code, which favors vocabulary close to the project's. History questions balance part of this, but they favor files that change often.
Caller answers use find_references when the question carries the identifier. On a natural language question, the agent has to discover that name first.
Ragnar cannot say something does not exist: it returns the closest match.
The comparison with v0 covers only 5 repositories, because indexing on a CPU took hours.

On Portuguese questions, the evidence reached the context in 4 of 17, against 7 of 17 in the 2026-11-01 run and 10 of 17 for grep. The right file was in the top 10 in 14 of them in both runs. Part of the drop comes from screen words: "tela" also searches form and frm, so .dfm forms rise and, in one HeidiSQL question, push the right unit out of the top 10. The expansion stays because it helps large Delphi codebases, where questions describe the screen.

With the real agent, the Ragnar mode read more context than in the 2026-11-01 run (median 41.8k tokens, before 35.9k), against 30.2k without Ragnar. The difference is in checking: after searching Ragnar, the agent used more Grep (1.16 per question, before 0.56) and more Read (0.58, before 0.30). The cause was not measured.
Reranker, multi-query, HyDE and contextual retrieval were not tested: they need models that did not run here.
v0 had aggregate results visible during the work, but no tuning used holdout results.
next: Repeat on a large monorepo, with thousands of files, where grep and reads cost more.
Measure sessions that edit code, not only questions.
Test a light local reranker, because the remaining gain is in the order of the first results.
Grow the set of Portuguese questions: 17 curated questions cannot tell a real loss from noise.
